title: Ideal-power quotient comparison for a single closed immersion
statement: Let $X$ and $Z$ be schemes, $J$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on $X$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], $n\in\mathbb N$, and $j:Z\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with kernel $J^n$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Let $a:j^*\dashv j_*$ be any supplied tensor-pullback adjunction [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, the recursively defined quotient $Q_n(F)$ with projection $q_n(F)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] admits an isomorphism $e:Q_n(F)\cong j_*j^*F$ satisfying $e\circ q_n(F)=\eta_{a,F}$. This assertion concerns one immersion and one module only; it asserts no inverse-system, transition, or naturality construction.

source.place: Lemma 087T (lemma-i-star-equivalence), equation 0880 (equation-completion-functor); closed-immersion unit quotient calculation of Modules, Lemma 08KS

proof.text: Prove monicity of the recursively constructed power inclusion by two-step induction: the zero power is the identity, the first power is the ideal inclusion, and each further inclusion is an image inclusion followed by the preceding monomorphism. On each affine U the proved ideal_times_quasiCoherent_affine_sections formula identifies the inclusion range with J(U)^n for positive n; the zero-power identity has the whole ring as range. IdealSheafData.range_toModulesι_app gives the same ranges for (J^n).toModulesι. Thus the recursive inclusion followed by (J^n).toPushforwardSubscheme is zero on affine opens, and hence zero everywhere by sheaf separatedness. Lift through its kernel (J^n).toModules. The resulting map is monic because its composite with the ideal inclusion is monic. It is surjective on each affine open by equal ranges and injectivity of the ideal inclusion. The public isIso_of_bijective_app_of_basis criterion makes this kernel lift an isomorphism. No quasi-coherence of F is needed; n=0, zero/unit ideals, empty schemes and zero modules require no extra hypotheses.

source.place: Lemma 087T (lemma-i-star-equivalence), equation 0880 (equation-completion-functor); closed-immersion unit quotient calculation of Modules, Lemma 08KS

proof.text: Rewrite J^n as ker(j) using hj. Tensor the inclusion-preserving power isomorphism with F. The two multiplication morphisms commute with this isomorphism and the identity on F by comp_whiskerRight. Apply cokernelImageι, cokernel.mapIso, and the inverse of cokernelImageι to obtain an isomorphism of the two image-inclusion cokernels. The cokernel projection identities show that it preserves the quotient projection. The existing closedImmersion_unit_quotient theorem supplies an isomorphism from the latter cokernel to j_*j^*F, normalized by its canonical adjunction unit.

proof.text: Compose with the pushforward of the component of adj.leftAdjointUniq a. The equation Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app gives precisely the unit of the supplied adjunction a after the quotient projection. All three isomorphisms and the two projection identities are combined in the Lean proof; no new auxiliary statements are left unproved.

mathlib_searches.query: A closed immersion with kernel the nth power of an ideal identifies the quotient module by that ideal power with pushforward of pullback, normalized by the unit

For a closed immersion with kernel J to the nth power, the quotient of a sheaf module by J to the nth power is canonically isomorphic to pushforward of pullback, with quotient projection equal to the adjunction unit

from.place: Completion comparison, step 1: identify the ideal-power quotient with pushforward of restriction, preserving the supplied unit.

lean.statement:
theorem closedImmersion_power_quotient {X Z : Scheme.{v}} (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (n : ℕ) (j : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hj : j.ker = J ^ n)
    (a : Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback j ⊣ Scheme.Modules.pushforward j)
    (F : X.Modules) :
    ∃ e : formalModuleQuotient J n F ≅
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward j).obj ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback j).obj F),
      formalModuleQuotientπ J n F ≫ e.hom = a.unit.app F
